purpose: Customer evidence, reusable research context and the next research question

policy.comparability: Compare conclusions only when business question, population, geography, period and method are sufficiently aligned. No automatic pooling or statistical significance from cohort means.

sources.title: US portal access and use, 2024
sources.method: HINTS 7; probability sampling; weighted national estimates
sources.summary: Portal use is widespread, while multiple portals create a useful research question about information fragmentation.
sources.limitations: National context; not a Quest customer sample. Measures have different bases and are not a single response distribution.

statistics.label: Accessed a portal at least once in the past year
Used an app to organize portals

sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Patient preferences for immediate results
sources.population: Patient portal users at four academic medical centers
sources.summary: Most respondents preferred immediate release. Higher worry after abnormal results can coexist with that preference.
sources.limitations: Self-selected portal users; older and predominantly English-speaking sample. Not representative of all patients or Quest customers. Question-specific denominators differ.

statistics.label: Reported increased worry after abnormal results
statistics.question: Result-related worry

statistics.label: Reported increased worry after normal results
statistics.question: Result-related worry

sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Hospital interoperability, 2023
sources.sample: Sample base not extracted in this source card
sources.summary: Information exchange capability and routine use are different measures. Lower-resource hospitals exchanged less frequently.
sources.limitations: Hospital-level reporting; not laboratory-specific or customer perceptions. At-least-sometimes and routine thresholds must not be treated as contradictory.

statistics.label: All four exchange domains at least sometimes

sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Patient-friendly results and subsequent messaging
sources.population: Patients receiving common outpatient laboratory results at Vanderbilt
sources.summary: Patient-friendly educational material was not associated with a clinically meaningful overall reduction in messages within 24 hours of result review.
sources.limitations: Single-center observational study. These percentages use results, not patients, as their denominator. Do not generalize workload effects to Quest.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Physician digital health research, 2022
sources.summary: Physicians assessed clinical benefit, reimbursement, liability and practice fit when considering digital tools.
sources.limitations: Broad digital health context; not diagnostic supplier preference. Older fieldwork should be reviewed before applying to current customer decisions.

statistics.label: Saw an advantage for patient care

sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Consumer requirements for laboratory portals
sources.method: Questionnaire with closed and open items; affinity analysis
sources.summary: Participants favored portal access but identified issues with usability, completeness and clarity of result displays.
sources.limitations: Small local sample; not a US prevalence estimate. University research summary links the primary JMIR paper; no transcript passages are held here.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Review of laboratory-result presentation
sources.summary: Visual reference ranges and color bars improved some perception and usability outcomes; evidence on actions and recall was sparse.
sources.limitations: Heterogeneous quality and outcomes; most studies used mock results. Does not establish clinical benefit or reduced messaging for a particular service.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: GP experiences of diagnostic-result communication
sources.method: Purposive sampling; semi-structured interviews; thematic analysis
sources.summary: GPs described setting expectations, adapting explanations to patients and balancing efficiency with patient participation. Jargon and misinterpretation were communication concerns.
sources.limitations: Dutch primary-care context; not Quest customers or US health-system executives. Participant and interview counts differ because one interview included two GPs. The source contains transcripts excerpts; no private transcripts are imported here.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Quest Comprehensive Insights
sources.summary: Quest describes analytics covering core-laboratory, Quest and third-party testing patterns.
sources.limitations: Supplier description supports a capability comparison, not awareness, preference, satisfaction or proven customer outcomes.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Quest Essential Insights
sources.summary: Quest describes reporting and analytics for laboratory testing sent to Quest.
sources.limitations: Product positioning is not evidence of customer preference or unmet needs.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Quanum Lab Services Manager
sources.summary: Quest describes online ordering, results and laboratory-service management tools.
sources.limitations: Published service features do not establish ease of use or customer satisfaction.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: Visiun integration options
sources.summary: Visiun describes deployment alternatives and integrations with laboratory information systems.
sources.limitations: Evaluate stated options against customer implementation requirements; no customer preference data are supplied.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: ARUP AnalyticsDx Sendout
sources.summary: The guide describes sendout reporting for volume, spend, turnaround, exceptions, utilization and exports.
sources.limitations: Guide functionality is not a customer experience study. Confirm data coverage and implementation details before like-for-like comparison.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

sources.title: MayoACCESS ordering and reporting
sources.summary: Mayo describes ordering, results retrieval and utilization reporting, including compatible laboratory-system connections.
sources.limitations: Supplier descriptions cannot establish awareness, consideration, reasons for preference or switching rates.
sources.approval: Public source reviewed; not Quest research approval

methodology_checks: Record sponsor and research conductor separately.
Retain the business question, exact instrument and answer options.
Document population, recruitment, sampling, geography and collection period.
Preserve subgroup bases, weighting, missing responses and question-level denominators.
Keep qualitative excerpts linked to their source passage and coding context.
Explain uncertainty, limitations and any model used for precision.

comparability_notes.title: Preference and worry can coexist
comparability_notes.reason: Immediate-release preference and worry after abnormal results are separate outcomes; this is not a contradictory finding.

comparability_notes.title: Capability is different from routine use
comparability_notes.reason: At least sometimes and routinely use different thresholds. Do not label the 70% and 43% estimates a conflict.

comparability_notes.title: Usability and messaging are different outcomes
comparability_notes.reason: Presentation experiments and real-world messaging involve different interventions, settings and outcomes. Their findings cannot be directly pooled.

comparability_notes.title: Preserve stakeholder and country context
comparability_notes.reason: Dutch GP interviews explain professional concerns; US patient survey percentages answer different questions. They are not a matched physician-versus-executive comparison.
